interface: Oil pressure → the PMU's fuel-pump gate
today: the 12A's C-09 resistive sender, PMU-excited through 100 Ω in the PMU box
at_the_swap: The LS oil-pressure sensor's signal is pinned into L1-E1 8 of the swap leg (LW16), the same cavity: the PMU's A7 gate and the ICU keep reading it at the node. A resistive sender keeps the 100 Ohm pull-up; a 0-5 V transducer takes the ECU's 5 V and sensor ground spliced in the bay (LW20, LW21) and the pull-up comes out at N39 (the sensor bought decides, K4, confirm). Never the ECU's CAN value. An open reading is zero oil pressure and stops the pump after the prime (electrical D-461): the gate's comparison follows the sensor - a resistive sender reads pressure BELOW its OIL_MIN count, a 0-5 V transducer ABOVE it - and with a transducer an open or out-of-range signal must still read as zero pressure, so the swap's gate is re-set at commissioning with the sensor in hand
